read_only_proof: This HARNESS is read-only — it opens each member's existing store and reads it. The store it read was re-indexed by hand immediately before the run (see generation.index_built_on): all 84 members, `logos index` per member from a binary built on this worktree's branch point (merged sprint-69 Iteration 1), exit 0 on every one, 0 failures. 25 member stores were rewritten and 59 were already current, which is what an incremental re-index over an already-warm estate does. It is stated here rather than implied, because a figure whose index generation is unattributable is the defect this artifact exists to prevent. Two readings of this generation were taken by two sessions: S-398 T2 re-indexed all 84 members (exit 0 on every one; 7,895 files / 93,838 nodes / 102,427 edges in 67 s) and read the estate twice, 34 minutes apart, with all 1034 reference rows byte-identical between them; S-403 T1 then re-read the same store. The two agree on every figure except `resolved_cross_service_edges`, which is the defect S-403 T1 fixed and is recorded in `generations`.

generation.why: Refusal rows and configuration-bound targets are both written at INDEX time, and so are the tree-sitter invocation queries S-402 T1 narrowed. generation.refresh_procedure: At the sprint-review human gate, on a binary built from this sprint's merged main: (1) `logos init --workspace --yes` at ~/source/pec-services if the estate is not enrolled — this re-enrols the root and spawns the detached warm supervisor that indexes the 84 members (~43 s to return; a root `logos index` covers the ROOT ONLY, 3 files, and that is correct). On an already-enrolled estate a per-member `logos index` sweep is enough and is what the reading above used. (2) Wait for `.logos.workspace.warm.json` to report every member warm. (3) Re-run this harness with `LOGOS_REF_WORKSPACE=~/source/pec-services LOGOS_BASELINE_WRITE=1 cargo test -p logos-core --test coverage_headline_baseline -- --nocapture`, which rewrites the `measurement` block below. (4) Restate the `deltas` entries whose status is `pending-reindex` as `observed`, with the figures the run produced. (5) Re-record the estate figures restated in prose OUTSIDE this artifact — nothing tests them, so they rot silently: docs/howto/commands.md (worked examples + the config-bound paragraph), logos-core/src/federation/coverage.rs (`by_intake` and `resolved_cross_service_edges` field docs), logos-core/src/federation/reach.rs (`resolved_cross_service_edges` and `spec_conformance_measured` field docs), mcp/src/server.rs (both tool descriptions), web/src/api_v1.rs, web/ui/src/api/types.ts. (6) Commit the artifact and the finding beside it.
generation.figures_the_refresh_would_change: DISCHARGED — every figure below is observed rather than predicted. Two successive refreshes are now on the record. The first (S-397 T2) verified its own prediction: 131 = 87 `base-url-runtime` refusals + 44 `config-bound` rows, with `resolved_cross_service_edges` staying 0 and `egress_resolution` moving off 0.000 to 0.032 (5 of 155). The second (this one) carries sprint-69 Iteration 1: the egress denominator FELL 155 -> 117 because S-402 T1 removed 26 captured Go non-calls, and the bound egress count ROSE 5 -> 15 because S-398 T1's qualified-receiver hop resolved ten more targets. Neither of those is S-403 T1's doing; S-403 T1's own effect is the headline moving 0 -> 15 over that same index, and it changes no classification and no resolution. The denominator's -38 decomposes as -26 (S-402 T1's smaller captured population, all 26 in hermodr-mirror, the estate's one Go member, whose captured client-call sites went 37 -> 11) and -12 (rows S-398 T1 admitted whose resolved template names a service with no provider in this workspace, which ADR-53 holds outside the denominator). The two movements are NOT summed anywhere.

headline_reading: FIFTEEN cross-service edges in this estate are resolved from a captured call site, over 117 captured egress sites (0.128) — while the retired bound_ratio reads 0.278 on the same data and the pooled `bound` reads 96. 81 of those 96 are contract-surface matches (an OpenAPI operation matched to a controller route) and the other 15 are the configuration-bound client calls. Until S-403 T1 this same payload published the headline as 0 beside `5 of 155 egress sites resolved` in ONE sentence: the edge count carried a `config-bound` exclusion that the rate's numerator did not (CR-127). NOTE what the 15 is not: the bridge draws NO invocation `BridgeEdge` for any of them — `logos xservice route-providers` returns 81 edges, all contract-surface — because the bridge keys a consumer on its RAW ledger target and the coverage tier resolves the placeholder. That second quantity rides on the reachability payload as `coverage.bridge_invocation_edges`, and it is 0.

S-374.story: The HTTP client-call arm records its refusals
S-374.effect: NOW OBSERVED. The 2026-09-13 re-index wrote 131 route/invocation rows where the 1.4.7 store held 1 — the workspace-wide figure S-374 recorded, landing at the upper end of the predicted 115-131 range exactly as the prediction said an index run would. 87 of them are `base-url-runtime` refusals and the other 44 are S-397 T1's configuration-bound rows, so the `unbound` column rose by 87 rather than by 131: the prediction's magnitude is confirmed and its split was not foreseen, because S-397 T1 had not been written when it was made. `egress_resolution_measured` 54 -> 155 and `spec_conformance_measured` 282 -> 383; `spec_conformance_ratio` 0.287 -> 0.225. `resolved_cross_service_edges` stayed 0 as predicted.

S-375.story: The client-call detector gate is receiver-grained, not file-grained
S-375.effect: ZERO change to every figure here, and that zero is a measured result rather than an absence. The narrowing removed 4 Java sites, all verified false positives (three list-index accesses and a cookie-map put), none of which emitted a reference: the workspace-wide genuine `http-client-call` reference count is 1 before and 1 after. Its real effect is on S-374's denominator on the NEXT index: against a file-grained gate, refusal recording would have written 4 ledger rows for a list index and a cookie put, so the range above would have been 4 rows wider at each end — the 'manufactures a coverage denominator out of ordinary code' hazard CR-120 §7 names, avoided.
S-375.evidence: sprint-impl-66.md, S-375 reference-workspace measurement table (before/after 98 -> 94 Java sites, 1 -> 1 workspace emitted)

S-377.story: Coverage reports its intake on every row

S-403.story: The resolved-edge headline agrees with its payload (this story)
S-403.effect: `resolved_cross_service_edges` 0 -> 15 and `resolved_edges_summary` "0 resolved cross-service edges; egress resolution 0.032 (5 of 155 …)" -> "15 resolved cross-service edges; egress resolution 0.128 (15 of 117 egress sites resolved)".
